Weightless at the Top

Self‑test

…

There is ONE weightless crest: apparent weight at the top of a vertical circle of radius r goes to ZERO at crest speed v² = g·r — equivalently crest angular rate ω₀ = √(g/r). The coaster EARNS that crest speed by FALLING from height h = 2.5r (v_top² = 2g(h−2r) = g·r); the ferris is DRIVEN to it by a motor (N_top = m(g − ω²r) = 0 at ω₀). With the live shared r = 9 and g = 9.81, that crest speed² is 88.29. The g·r is the whole story — no smuggled factor (three byte-exact === identities). Both parent cores are imported byte-for-byte and the two adapters share no code: the IMPOSED adapter names only the ferris's fns, the EARNED adapter only the coaster's.
a cross · The Coaster × The Ferris Wheel

Two rides reach the same weightless top by opposite means. On the left a coaster bead is released from a height and EARNS its crest speed by falling — the energy of the drop alone. On the right a ferris gondola is DRIVEN to crest speed by a motor turning the wheel. At the very top, apparent weight obeys one threshold: it hits zero when the crest speed² equals g·r. Raise the release height to 2.5 r and dial the spin to ω₀, and the two felt-weight needles sweep to the same zero from opposite mechanisms — one fell to it, one was driven to it.

Raise the release height toward 2.5 r — a gold detent eases it onto the just-clears mark — and press ▷ release: at h ≥ 2.5r the bead clears the top and floats free; below it the rail can't hold the bead and it detaches, arcing off ballistic. Dial the spin toward ω₀ (a faint detent marks the float speed): below ω₀ the crest still presses; at ω₀ it unloads to 0; past ω₀ it swings negative and the lap-bar lights. The shared crest needle reads both: cool = the coaster's earned crest, gold = the ferris's driven crest. When both cross the SAME zero in one beat the mark blooms. Slide mass and the ferris force moves while the zero never does. Toggle sound for a soft chime on the meeting (mutable, never load-bearing).

what this proves, and what it doesn't

  • One threshold, two mechanisms. The coaster floats when its crest speed² (read from the-coaster's own integrated trace) equals g·r; the ferris floats when its crest reading N_top = m(g − ω²r) (read from ferris-wheel's own law) hits 0 at ω₀ = √(g/r). Both target the SAME crest speed² = g·r. With the live shared r = 9 that is 88.29, and the imposed crest speed² meets it to machine ε (~1.4e-14).
  • The g·r is the whole story (no fudge). Three byte-exact identities: the driven crest unloads to N_top(ω₀) === 0; the float root has no smuggled factor (ω₀²·r === g); the just-clears release EARNS exactly the float speed (2g(2.5r − 2r) === g·r). And both rides feel the SAME one gravity (CO.G === FW.G).
  • Earned, through the real parent. The cool needle is not a formula — it is the crest speed read off the-coaster's own energy stepper, integrated frame by frame. At h = 2.5r the integrated crest v²/(g·r) lands on 1 to the sample floor (~1e-16) and the felt needle reads ≈ 0. (A loose bound by design — the discretized scan can't hit the crest sample exactly; the machine-ε bounds live on the analytic identities.)
  • The negative controls bite (touchable), each from its own authority. A just-clearing release (h = 2.5r) does NOT detach; a hair below (2.49r) DOES — the bead leaves the rail at a real angle and arcs off (the-coaster's detach verdict). And a sub-float spin still presses: at half ω₀ the crest reads ¾g > 0, not weightless. Neither is clamped — the ferris crest sails PAST zero into the lap-bar's negative pull.
  • Mass-invariant zero. Slide the rider's mass and the ferris's crest force scales with it, but the float threshold has no mass — ω₀ = √(g/r) — and the coaster crest is mass-free too. The needles' shared ZERO never moves. The aesthetic constants are not proven; the shared weightless crest is.
